sections.heading: Find the patterns that inform your decisions
sections.body:
Use machine learning to estimate future outcomes, score risk and detect unusual patterns in enterprise data. Start from a decision, compare models with a meaningful baseline, and validate performance before operational use.

Churn, demand, fraud, loan default and equipment failure each need different data and evaluation choices. More data or retraining does not automatically make a model better; review performance, limitations and the cost of a wrong prediction.

[Explore Data & AI](/services/data-ai).

sections.heading: Prediction, scoring and forecasting
sections.description: Agree the decision owner, model output and evaluation needs before development. These enterprise use cases are starting points, not promises of accuracy or business return.

items.title: Customer & churn models
items.description: Support retention teams with customer segments and churn scores.
items.bullets:
Data — customer history and outcome definitions
Evaluation — baseline and intervention timing
Decision — cases to review for retention

items.title: Operational anomaly detection
items.description: Highlight unusual operational patterns for investigation by an accountable team.
items.bullets:
Data — expected patterns and known incidents
Evaluation — false alerts and missed signals
Decision — what needs investigation

items.title: Fraud & risk scoring
items.description: Support fraud and credit teams with scores for review, including loan default risk.
items.bullets:
Data — reviewed labels and outcome windows
Evaluation — precision, recall and error cost
Decision — investigation or further review

items.title: Demand & maintenance forecasting
items.description: Give planning and maintenance teams forecasts or failure estimates with stated limits.
items.bullets:
Data — demand or equipment history
Evaluation — time-aware tests and forecast error
Decision — planning or maintenance action

sections.heading: Evaluate carefully and use predictions responsibly
sections.description: Agree the decision, baseline and cost of error. Define development, integration and operational scope without treating explainability as evidence of accuracy.

items.title: Define the decision — baseline and error cost
items.description: Agree the user, target outcome, prediction window and action the output informs. Set a meaningful baseline, success measure and cost-of-error trade-off before selecting a model.

items.title: Prepare the data — reviewed evaluation split
items.description: Review access, quality, labels and representativeness. Agree leakage-safe training and evaluation separation, using time-aware splits where the decision requires them.

items.title: Evaluate the model — thresholds and limitations
items.description: Compare with the baseline using agreed measures, such as forecast error or precision/recall. Document thresholds, false positives, missed cases, interpretable outputs and limitations before release approval.

items.title: Integrate and operate — scoring and monitoring owners
items.description: Agree the scoring interface and workflow with integration teams. Scope monitoring, drift review, retraining decisions and rollback; name operating and approval owners, and evaluate changes before reuse.

sections.heading: A model around your decision, not a generic score
sections.description: Our ML service defines, adapts, evaluates, integrates and operates models around your decision within an agreed scope. Reusable accelerators provide selected starting points, not validated results for your data.

items.title: Predictive Analytics Suite
items.description: Reusable starting models for churn and segmentation, demand forecasting, fraud and anomaly detection, and loan default prediction.

items.title: Digital Twin Suite
items.description: For asset models, forecasting simulation, inventory optimisation and real-time monitoring. Scenario simulation is a separate scope; an ML model is not automatically a digital twin.

items.title: Power BI + AI/ML
items.description: Present evaluated model outputs through predictive dashboards and risk-scoring visuals. Data platforms and reporting work can support this presentation layer.

sections.note: Agree data readiness, adaptation, evaluation, deployment and commercial scope. Accelerators are reusable delivery IP, not automatic inclusions or a substitute for validating your model.

sections.heading: A prediction evaluated in context
sections.description: For a demand-planning model, agree the evidence below before operational use. This is an example evaluation pattern, not a client case or an achieved performance claim.

items.title: Baseline and evaluation record
items.description: Define the planning horizon, historical data window and baseline forecast. Use an appropriate time-aware evaluation split; record forecast error and the limits of historical data.

items.title: Controlled operational use
items.description: Agree a model/evaluation record, permitted data access and planner review. Scope the scoring interface and security validation before operational predictions are used.

items.title: Monitoring and decision ownership
items.description: Name drift, retraining and rollback owners. Review technical performance separately from business impact, with the agreed planning workflow and operating evidence.

sections.note: Describe the outcome to predict or score, available historical data and the cost of a wrong prediction. Do not upload confidential datasets through the enquiry form.

sections.heading: Check feasibility before committing to a model
sections.description: Agree an initial feasibility scope and the measures that will inform a go/no-go decision. Select commercial and support arrangements around confirmed responsibilities.

items.title: Is our historical data sufficient?
items.description: Assess quality, coverage, labels and relevance to the prediction window first. The question is whether the data supports a meaningful baseline and evaluation, not simply whether there is a large volume of it.

items.title: How will we know whether the model is useful?
items.description: Compare with an agreed baseline and review errors in the intended decision context. Technical measures such as forecast error or precision/recall are not business outcomes. Review the cost of errors, workflow use and limitations before operational adoption.

items.title: Can models support security anomaly detection?
items.description: Security anomalies are one possible use case, not the definition of the ML service. Scope specialist security requirements and response responsibilities with Cyber Security teams. This service also covers customer, operational, fraud, risk and forecasting decisions.

items.title: How do deployment and ongoing support fit commercially?
items.description: Time & Materials suits feasibility and evolving model development; Fixed Price suits defined scope and acceptance criteria. Dedicated Team or Managed Service models require agreed capacity, monitoring and operating ownership. Outcome-Based terms require outcomes that can be agreed and evidenced. Confirm support scope rather than assume it is included.

items.title: What should we bring to the first discussion?
items.description: Describe the target outcome, available historical data, decision owner and cost of error, without sending confidential datasets. Agree feasibility and scoping next steps with the team. An NDA can be arranged where required.
